title: WSPR Signal-to-Noise Distribution
dataSources: APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), WSPR spots (`wspr:spot`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`), NOAA APT captures (`noaa:apt`), meteor-scatter pings (`meteorscatter:ping`), SSTV images (`sstv:image`).
app: Software-defined radio and ham-radio stations — APRS igate, WSPR beacon, NOAA weather-satellite (APT) receiver, meteor-scatter monitor, and SSTV decoder — logging to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=wspr:spot
| eval snr_bucket=case(snr<-25,"very weak",snr<-15,"weak",snr<-5,"fair",1=1,"strong")
| stats count by band snr_bucket
| sort band
description: Breaks your received WSPR reports into signal-strength bands so you can judge how well your antenna hears faint signals.
value: The share of very-weak decodes you catch is a real measure of receiver sensitivity, useful for comparing antennas objectively.
implementation: Ingest WSPR spots with signal-to-noise values; review the strength distribution per band.
visualization: Stacked bar chart of signal strength buckets by band.
grandmaExplanation: It sorts the radio signals you receive by how faint they are, showing how good your antenna is at hearing weak ones.
